topic: empirical reply-to-proposition alignment in email and dialogue, focusing on partial replies, multiple questions, unanswered questions, and multi-proposition antecedents
executive_summary: Across 26 papers, the strongest empirical conclusion is structural rather than proposition-semantic: reply and reference relations are frequently non-bijective, and systems must be able to represent no link, one link, and multiple antecedents or targets. Dialogue and email studies also show that adjacency alone is unreliable and that thread, discourse, segmentation, and conversational context materially help alignment. Abstract-anaphora work establishes that antecedents may be clauses, discourse segments, or composite material, while annotation studies document overlapping, disputed, or multiple acceptable antecedents. However, the corpus still does not validate proposition-level partial-answer, approval, rejection, or commitment scope in authentic workplace communication. Existing QA datasets generally align sentences, utterances, paragraphs, or grouped segments. Consequently, all five carried gaps remain open, including the combined annotation contract and msgloom-specific uncertainty/cost policy.
themes: Reply and reference structure is not reliably one-to-one: zero-link, one-to-many, many-to-one, and multi-parent relations are empirically documented [doi-10-1609-aaai-v33i01-3301134; doi-10-18653-v1-d15-1109; doi-10-3233-aic-2012-0516].

Antecedents can be non-nominal and larger than a single entity mention, including clauses, sentential material, discourse segments, and sometimes combinations of several units [doi-10-1093-jos-17-1-51; doi-10-1162-coli-a-00327; manual-be69c3aa17].

Partial answerhood is well motivated semantically, but the reviewed empirical QA-alignment literature generally does not operationalize proposition-level partial-answer scope [doi-10-3765-sp-5-6; manual-5a32708675; doi-10-3233-aic-2012-0516].

Antecedent boundaries are often difficult or ambiguous to delimit, with overlapping, multiple acceptable, and alternative antecedents documented in several annotation studies [doi-10-18653-v1-s15-1035; manual-7743c50805; manual-be69c3aa17].

Structural and conversational context improves alignment, but useful locality assumptions vary materially by task and domain [manual-a6314f615a; doi-10-1609-aaai-v33i01-3301134; doi-10-18653-v1-2022-emnlp-main-778].
Linguistic and syntactic constraints are useful but defeasible rather than universally reliable; their effect depends on the target construction and dataset [1706.02256; doi-10-3115-v1-d14-1056].

Cross-domain robustness is a recurring problem: methods specialized for one corpus or discourse convention can degrade when transferred to another [doi-10-1109-icaicta63815-2024-10762999; doi-10-18653-v1-2021-codi-sharedtask-1].

findings.statement: Empirical dialogue and email data require non-bijective alignment representations: one answer can correspond to multiple questions, one question can receive multiple answers, and a discourse move can attach to multiple prior units.

findings.statement: Explicit no-link outcomes are empirically necessary: some answer-side utterances answer no preceding question, some anaphoric expressions have no identifiable linguistic antecedent, and annotated email threads can contain questions with no corresponding answer.

The reviewed empirical QA-alignment studies do not establish proposition-level partial-reply resolution. Their principal alignment units are utterances, sentences, paragraphs, topic segments, or multi-sentence groups, and several papers explicitly note that finer partial-answer scope is not represented.

Several interrogatives in one turn cannot automatically be interpreted as several independent outstanding obligations, because observed multiple-question sequences can be repetitions or reformulations used to manage comprehension.

Exact abstract-antecedent boundaries are often difficult or ambiguous to delimit rather than uniformly well defined: studies report overlapping spans, disagreement about boundaries, multiple acceptable antecedents, alternative interpretations, and problems with discontinuous antecedents.

Composite and multi-unit antecedents are linguistically plausible and are represented in discourse and abstract-anaphora analyses, but this corpus does not directly validate multi-proposition response scope in authentic workplace communication.

findings.statement: Locality is strongly task dependent. Discourse-deictic antecedents in the CODI-CRAC dialogue evaluation were usually nearby, while email QA work documents delayed answers and event-reference work reports substantially larger candidate spaces and longer-distance links; therefore a short universal search window is not supported.

Alignment quality benefits from discourse and conversation structure beyond pairwise lexical similarity: email thread features, conversation-level dependencies, discourse attachment structure, and improved question/answer segmentation all provide measurable gains in their respective datasets.

Syntactic and lexico-syntactic cues are useful but task dependent and defeasible: explicit syntax helps some shell-noun settings, while broader abstract-anaphora settings and syntactically versatile shell nouns can perform better with less restrictive constraints.

Formal question theories support a distinction between complete resolution and contributions that are only partial answers, but these theoretical accounts do not constitute empirical validation of a proposition-level reply-state taxonomy for workplace communication.

contradictions.topic: One-to-one alignment assumptions versus empirically non-bijective reply structure
contradictions.note: Some QA-alignment pipelines operationalize correspondence through one-to-one matching or grouped pairings, whereas customer-service, email, and multiparty-dialogue data contain one-to-many, many-to-one, and multi-parent structures. This is best interpreted as a mismatch between some benchmark/model assumptions and broader observed discourse structure, not as a universal contradiction across identical tasks.

contradictions.topic: Strong locality in discourse deixis versus delayed or longer-distance antecedence in other tasks
contradictions.note: The discourse-deixis evaluation finds most antecedents within a few utterances, while email QA and event-reference studies document delayed or longer-distance dependencies. manual-5c0971730d uses a short search window as a modeling assumption and therefore is not evidence that antecedents are empirically local. The combined evidence supports task- and domain-dependent locality rather than one universal distance rule.

contradictions.topic: Single-gold antecedent evaluation versus documented ambiguity and overlap
contradictions.note: Benchmarking benefits from concrete gold links, but multiple annotation studies document overlapping, alternative, or multiple acceptable abstract antecedents. This creates a methodological tension between exact-link scoring and the ambiguity present in the underlying phenomenon.

gaps.description: Direct empirical evidence is still missing for proposition-level agreement, rejection, approval, clarification, and answer scope in authentic workplace email or enterprise chat, especially cases where one short response applies to only part of a preceding message.
gaps.suggested_query: "reply scope" email dialogue proposition agreement approval rejection workplace communication

gaps.description: A validated annotation and evaluation scheme is still missing for mapping workplace responses to exact proposition or span targets while representing exact, partial, ambiguous, unsupported, discontinuous, multiple-antecedent, and explicit no-link cases. Individual requirements are supported by the literature, but the combined msgloom annotation contract has not been validated.

Direct evidence remains insufficient for aligning replies to one or more questions when a preceding workplace message contains multiple questions, requests, or alternatives, including proposition-level detection of questions that remain unanswered.
gaps.suggested_query: "question answer alignment" dialogue "multiple questions" partial answer unanswered questions

gaps.description: It remains open whether and how a workplace response should be modeled as targeting a composite or multi-proposition antecedent. The corpus supports composite abstract discourse referents and multi-unit discourse antecedents, but does not directly evaluate multi-proposition reply scope in work communication.
gaps.suggested_query: "multi-antecedent" propositional anaphora dialogue composite discourse referent reply

gaps.description: The appropriate msgloom policy for uncertainty-driven abstention, ambiguity, missing antecedents, and asymmetric error costs remains unvalidated. The literature supports explicit no-link outcomes and preservation of ambiguous or multiple antecedents, but it does not establish confidence thresholds or the relative cost of over-broad approval/commitment links versus unresolved links.

actionable_insights: Directly evidenced annotation requirements can be adopted as inputs to an engineering prototype: support explicit no-link/None outcomes [doi-10-1609-aaai-v33i01-3301134; doi-10-1093-jos-17-1-51], multiple antecedents or parents [doi-10-18653-v1-d15-1109; doi-10-18653-v1-2023-eacl-main-247], non-nominal/discourse-segment antecedents [doi-10-1093-jos-17-1-51; manual-be69c3aa17], and alternative or overlapping antecedents [doi-10-18653-v1-s15-1035; manual-7743c50805]. Combining these into one workplace annotation/evaluation contract remains gap-2.

Treat proposition decomposition and per-proposition states such as resolved, partially addressed, unresolved, ambiguous, or unsupported as proposed msgloom design hypotheses to test, not as operations validated by the reviewed QA-alignment literature [manual-5a32708675; doi-10-3233-aic-2012-0516; doi-10-3765-sp-5-6].

For approval, agreement, rejection, or commitment handling, msgloom may adopt a conservative risk-management policy that avoids propagating a response to sibling propositions without target-specific evidence. This is a product safety policy, not an empirical conclusion from the literature; the cited work only motivates avoiding forced single-target links and preserving no-link, multiple-target, and ambiguous cases [doi-10-1609-aaai-v33i01-3301134; doi-10-18653-v1-s15-1035; doi-10-18653-v1-d15-1109].

Do not hard-code one universal antecedent-distance window. Use recency as a useful feature where appropriate, while preserving a mechanism for delayed or longer-distance candidates in email and other reference tasks [doi-10-18653-v1-2022-emnlp-main-778; manual-a6314f615a; manual-555fa5b6e8].

Evaluate the system in separable stages: candidate/unit detection, segmentation, link prediction, relation classification, and semantic completeness. Gold segmentation results in the Japanese assembly study show that better segmentation alone does not eliminate alignment errors [doi-10-1109-icaicta63815-2024-10762999].

Include dedicated benchmark strata for zero-link, one-to-one, one-to-many, many-to-one or multi-parent, delayed, overlapping-antecedent, and ambiguous cases rather than reporting only aggregate alignment F1 [doi-10-1609-aaai-v33i01-3301134; doi-10-18653-v1-d15-1109; doi-10-18653-v1-s15-1035].

Investigate evaluation with partial credit or alternative acceptable gold targets for abstract antecedents, because strict exact-link scoring can count overlapping or linguistically defensible alternatives as complete errors [doi-10-18653-v1-s15-1035; manual-be69c3aa17; manual-7743c50805].
confidence_summary: Confidence is high for the structural conclusions that reply/reference relations can have zero or multiple links, that non-nominal and discourse-segment antecedents occur, that exact abstract-antecedent boundaries can be difficult or multiply acceptable, and that discourse structure improves alignment in several datasets. Confidence is medium for transferring these mechanisms to workplace email because only a small subset of the corpus directly studies email and none validates proposition-level approval, rejection, commitment, or partial-answer scope in authentic enterprise communication. Confidence is low for any claim about msgloom-specific abstention thresholds, error-cost asymmetry, proposition-state taxonomies, or production accuracy; these remain engineering hypotheses or open academic questions.
limitations: The corpus mixes formal semantics, qualitative conversation analysis, anaphora, event coreference, discourse parsing, customer service, political assembly minutes, game chat, student forums, and email; transfer evidence should not be treated as direct workplace-email accuracy.

Several papers are available only through abstracts, limiting verification of corpus construction, annotation details, and error analyses [doi-10-1007-bf00983299; doi-10-1007-s10489-013-0481-1; doi-10-1016-j-pragma-2007-07-011; doi-10-1093-jos-17-1-51].
The empirical studies use incompatible units such as utterances, sentences, paragraphs, EDUs, topic segments, and QA groups, making aggregate performance numbers non-comparable across papers.
The corpus contains no direct benchmark for proposition-level approval, rejection, agreement, clarification, or commitment scope in authentic enterprise email or Teams-like communication.

Unanswered questions are present or inferable in several datasets, but most studies do not make proposition-level unanswered-question detection a primary evaluated task [manual-a6314f615a; doi-10-1007-s10489-013-0481-1; doi-10-1609-aaai-v33i01-3301134].

Composite abstract antecedents are supported by discourse and anaphora literature, but this does not establish how a workplace reply should be semantically distributed over propositions within such a composite target [manual-8b8a394daa; doi-10-18653-v1-d15-1109].
No reviewed paper validates the msgloom-specific cost tradeoff between over-broad state propagation and leaving a response unresolved.

gap_status.note: Email QA studies provide sentence- or paragraph-level pairing, and dialogue studies provide utterance/discourse attachment, but the corpus still lacks direct proposition-level evidence for agreement, rejection, approval, clarification, or partial response scope in authentic workplace communication.

The literature separately supports no-link outcomes, multiple and non-nominal antecedents, alternative interpretations, overlapping spans, and discontinuous antecedents, but no paper validates the complete workplace annotation/evaluation contract required by msgloom.

The new corpus adds strong evidence that multiple questions and non-bijective QA mappings occur, but available benchmarks still do not directly evaluate proposition-level partial answers and outstanding subquestions in workplace multi-question messages.

Composite, split, and multi-unit antecedents are supported in discourse/anaphora analyses, but this remains transfer or theoretical evidence rather than direct evaluation of a workplace response targeting several propositions as one semantic scope.

The corpus supports representing None/no-link cases and preserving ambiguous or multiple antecedents, but it does not validate uncertainty thresholds, abstention calibration, or msgloom's asymmetric risk model for over-broad versus unresolved approval and commitment links.
